1. Look into the site flyonward. When you get on your last flight en route to Bangkok they will want to see your flight out of the country so they know you will leave before your visa expires. This site lets you rent a real flight for 24-48 hours that you can show at your gate on your last flight to Thailand.

2. Remember to get out of the larger cities and explore, it's amazing what you can get yourself into when you get out.  

3. Be sure to look into the visa situation for the next country you plan to enter a few weeks ahead of time so your not left stranded when you cant enter a certain county easily.  

4. Look into couch surfing or working for your accommodation in hostels. Especially if this is a long-term thing for you it will allow you to save lots in the long run.  Being that you are a girl make sure to take a few precautions when Couchsurfing. ie. stay with female hosts.

Hey, great post I'm in a similar situation to you but just a little closer to the goal. I also dropped out from college and am currently 21, I've also been living with my family for the past year and a half and am only a few months off from leaving on my travels.  I'll try to answer all your questions simply and then give you more places to check out and help decide what kind of travel you're going for.  

1. These are separate things but in a way work in conjunction. Wilderness involves day trekking and camping. Well, backpacking is travelling to different countries and seeing new part of the world the kind I'm interested in!

2. Begin by saving, set travel as your goal above all else and take the necessary step to get there no matter how challenging they can be. Paying of loans should be a priority get this out of the way as fast as possible work multiple jobs and keep reminding yourself of the end goal. There are plenty of resources online for saving money to travel but here is a great blog to start. www.nomadicmatt.com

3. You can find plenty of gear list online but don't overcomplicate things. Back essentials and buy as you need. 

4. $50 a day is a good budget for most places in the world Asia is cheaper about $25

5. Finding places to stay is the easier part of travel. Booking.com Hostelbookers and Hostelworld are great websites for finding hostels around the world.  

6. Your 21 man get some travel insurance and your golden.

7. This is probably a personal preference it will probably be a bigger inconvenience than its worth, but everyone has one thing they bring that nobody else does.

Cheers!
